text:
maria: quick heads-up — after rolling int4 on the middle transformer blocks (embed + lm_head still fp8) we're seeing a weird KV throughput drop on 2xA100 pools. latency tail jumps ~20% at 99th.
aj: ugh. did you change kernel selector heuristics or quantization calibration at the same time?
maria: only the per-layer quant map. calibration ran but we excluded embedding and lm_head. no kernel selector changes.
devon: can you paste the profiler snippet? sounds like kernel thrash between int4 and fp8 paths during prefix queries.
maria: here — real short sample (token loop condensed):
```
kernel_selector: choose=int4_fast (layers 3-18)
kv_cache_hit: 0.82
avg_batch_size: 1.9
dispatch_latency_ms: 0.9 -> 3.2
kernel_switch_count: 84
cpu->gpu memcpy spikes at switch
```
sana: kernel_switch_count 84 per request is alarming. probably continuous batching is merging requests that hit different quant variants -> cache warmup + memcpy thrash.
aj: two quick mitigations to try: 1) add a short selector hysteresis so adjacent requests stick to previous kernel for N tokens; 2) prefer sticky routing for hot prefixes (small warmup windows).
maria: wrote a tiny config to test hysteresis:
```json
{"kernel_selector": {"hysteresis_tokens": 8, "prefer_same_variant": true}}
```
will spin a canary tonight.
devon: also check batching policy: if avg_batch_size ~1.9, we might be paying overheads from kernel rebinds. try batch_compaction: true and max_compact_time_ms: 6.
perf-bot: perf alert generated: service=redwood-runtime env=canary metric=kv_throughput drop=22% window=5m
sana: if that helps, we should consider an offline pass to mark sensitive layers that can't be safely quantized without routing penalties — e.g., top-3 attention layers where kv layout differs.
aj: agree. another option: keep KV layout unified (fp8-compatible packing) and convert compute to int4 via mixed path to avoid memcpy. more engineering but lower tail risk.
maria: note — calibration quality didn't fall for our eval set, so this is pure runtime perf, not accuracy.
devon: for the canary, capture these traces: kernel_switch_count, memcpy_bytes, dispatch_latency, kv_miss_ratio. add tagging by model_version and quant_map.
maria: executing canary now. will update with numbers tomorrow and attach a flamegraph if things still look bad. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
